theorems.title: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal

steps.content: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides. In such a figure, the opposite sides are always equal in length.
Draw a diagonal to form two triangles. By ASA congruence (Angle-Side-Angle), the two triangles are congruent. Therefore, corresponding parts (opposite sides) are equal.
If you know one side is 5cm, the opposite side must also be 5cm. Use this to solve for unknown lengths.
Used in engineering, architecture (like scissor lifts), and design patterns where parallel motion is required.

theorems.title: Diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular

steps.content: A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal. Its diagonals intersect at a 90-degree angle.
Since all sides are equal, the triangles formed by diagonals are congruent by SSS. The linear pair of angles at the center are equal, so they must be 90 degrees each.
Use Pythagoras theorem in the right-angled triangles formed by the diagonals to find side lengths or diagonal lengths.
Seen in diamond shapes on playing cards, traffic signs, and structural cross-bracing.
